\begin{abstract}
We revisit \emph{ordinary least squares}.
\end{abstract}

\section{Estimation}
\label{sec:est}
We estimate $\beta \in \R^p$ by
% a comment that should vanish
\emph{ordinary least squares}:
\begin{equation}
  \hat\beta = \argmin_b \|y - Xb\|^2 = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top y
  \label{eq:ols}
\end{equation}
Under \textbf{A1--A3}, \eqref{eq:ols} is unbiased~\cite{greene2012, hayashi}.
See Section~\ref{sec:est} and Theorem~\ref{thm:gm}.

\begin{align}
  \mathbb{E}[\hat\beta] &= \beta \label{eq:unbiased} \\
  \operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta) &= \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1} \nonumber
\end{align}

\begin{theorem}[Gauss--Markov]\label{thm:gm}
OLS is BLUE.
\end{theorem}

  \item Variance: $\sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}$, costs 5\% of \$10.
